$comment: 'One user action produces one request — no amplification.' A budget is raised
only with a recorded justification; the reviewer checklist treats a raised
budget as an architecture change, not a tuning knob.
Recordings are produced by the Playwright run (apps/web/e2e) and compared here.
A budgeted interaction with no recording FAILS: a broken e2e run must not be
able to satisfy the budget by producing nothing.
Every 'maxRequests' below is a MEASURED number, not a target. The measurement
is the recording in ./recordings/, produced by the real browser against the
real production bundle at both viewports.

interactions.description: Cold load of the application shell, to first settled connection state.
interactions.note: Document, JS bundle, CSS bundle, favicon, and the one /api/health call. Headroom is deliberate: this is a page load, not a user action.

interactions.description: User clicks 'Check again' in the connection panel.
interactions.note: I-10 in its strictest form. One click, one request. Any retry, revalidation, or telemetry beat would break this and is meant to.

interactions.description: User clicks 'New rule' to open the rule-authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, in the same strict form as catalogue-open-new-shift-type. A control labelled New must persist nothing before a completed form and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-002).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Save rule' and the server refuses it with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-002).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Save rule' and the server accepts it.
interactions.note: The write plus ONE invalidation refetch of the rule list. Two is the measured number, not a target: the list must reflect the new rule and the client does not synthesise it from the response. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-002).

interactions.description: User clicks 'New shift type' to open the authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, and the reason the invariant exists: a control labelled New must persist nothing before a completed form and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number here — this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports.

interactions.description: User clicks Save and the server refuses the shift type with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed and there is nothing new to fetch — which is what makes the two-request success budget below a property of the success path rather than of Save in general. Measured 1 at both viewports.

interactions.description: User fills every field on the activation form and does not submit.
interactions.note: I-13, on a credential-setting form. ZERO is the only correct number: a field that saved on change would put a half-typed password on the wire, and an activation form that wrote on mount would consume an invitation token nobody submitted. This budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-001).

interactions.description: User submits an empty activation form; the CLIENT refuses it.
interactions.note: A client-side pre-check that still called the server would be the amplification I-10 forbids, dressed as helpfulness. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-001).

interactions.description: User submits the password-reset request form.
interactions.note: I-10 in its strictest form: one submit, one POST. There is no read-back, because the response is deliberately identical whatever the server found — there is nothing to re-read. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-001).

interactions.description: User clicks Save and the server accepts the shift type (200).
interactions.note: TWO, ruled and justified — not an I-10 exception. The POST plus the server-authoritative list refetch is the PO-DEC-18 display posture: after a mutation the client re-reads what the SERVER says the list is, rather than patching its own cache from the response and rendering a view no server ever produced. The second request is therefore the invariant's intent (one action, one authoritative round trip to re-establish truth) rather than amplification of it — amplification is N requests for one action's WORK, and this is one write plus one read-back. A one-request alternative exists (POST returns the row; the client updates the list from it) and is recorded as a later-packet option; it is deliberately NOT implemented, because it moves the rendered list's authority to the client. Ruled by Fable on the OPUS-M2-004 escalation (packet 30 §6a as amended). Measured 2 at both viewports: POST .../catalogue/shift-types, then GET .../catalogue/shift-types.

interactions.description: User clicks 'Add a location' to open the authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, in the same strict form as catalogue-open-new-shift-type and rules-open-new-rule. A control labelled Add must persist nothing before a completed form, validation, and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User clicks Save and the server accepts the location (200).
interactions.note: The POST plus ONE server-authoritative list refetch, under the same PO-DEC-18 ruling the catalogue's accepted-save budget carries: after a mutation the client re-reads what the SERVER says the list is rather than patching its own cache and rendering a view no server produced. One write plus one read-back is not amplification. Measured 2 at both viewports: POST .../settings/locations, then GET .../settings/locations (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User acknowledges the published-schedule impact and saves a new group time zone (204).
interactions.note: The PUT plus ONE re-read of the settings, same ruling as above — and here the read-back is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the settings response carries the optimistic-concurrency token (groups.settings_version) that the next save must echo, so a client that patched its own cache would save against a version it invented. Measured 2 at both viewports: PUT .../settings/timezone, then GET .../settings (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User saves a time-zone change without acknowledging the published-schedule impact; the server refuses it with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed and there is nothing new to read — which is what makes the two-request success budget above a property of the success path rather than of Save in general. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-007).
